transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-05-21 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~57 minutes
Attendees: Maya Patel (Redwood AE), Connor Liu (Redwood SE), Rae Emerson (Redwood SE), Samira Khan (QuasarFlux CTO), Diego Ruiz (Platform Eng), Evelyn Park (Security), Liam O'Neill (Infra)

Summary (auto): Align on connector packaging and auth/KMS requirements for QuasarFlux hybrid listing. Next: share Helm chart example, run benchmarks, provide SOC2/KMS notes.

Topics: marketplace packaging, SAML/OIDC, service account model, KMS/HSM, audit logs, helm/CI, benchmark plan.

--- Transcript ---
[00:00] Maya Patel: hey everybody, thanks for joining. quick intro, i'm maya, i'm the AE on the QuasarFlux account. with me are connor and rae from our eng team. Samira over to you for a quick context of what you're trying to achieve?
[00:18] Samira Khan: yeah thanks maya. so high level, we want to list a QuasarFlux-managed connector in the Redwood marketplace and also support an on-prem adapter for our enterprise customers. functionality: auth integration with SSO, KMS for key material, and telemetry we can ingest into our observability stack. timeline is... ideally Q3 but pilot earlier.
[00:39] Diego Ruiz: and to add, our infra runs a mixture of EKS and a couple of bare-metal clusters; we want the connector to be deployable via Helm or a simple tarball for air-gapped customers.
[00:52] Connor Liu: got it. that's aligned with what we've done before. we'll need to map the packaging and the service account model. quick question: when you say KMS, are you expecting Redwood to use your KMS via an external key, or do you want us to ship with integrated KMS support where keys are customer-managed?
[01:12] Evelyn Park: we require customer-managed keys for any PII or model context. so integration with our HSM or cloud KMS is a must. also we need audit logs pushed to our SIEM.
[01:22] Rae Emerson: okay cool, so two things then: 1) KMS customer-managed (bring-your-own-key), and 2) audit logs / structured telemetry. on the listing side, we have a packaging checklist that includes a Helm chart, a container image with signed provenance, and a small integration test harness. i'll talk through that in a sec.
[01:40] Samira Khan: sounds good. what about network topology? we need private connectivity patterns — VPC peering vs private link vs gateway.
[01:50] Maya Patel: right we typically offer a couple of patterns: hosted via Redwood API when customers are okay with hosted inference, Redwood Dedicated for reserved pools, and Redwood Private for VPC/on-prem installs. for the marketplace listing, the packaging must support our Private deployment model if you want to address regulated customers.
[02:12] Diego Ruiz: note: for many of our customers the allowed egress is very limited. we need to ensure the connector can run fully air-gapped with a local model cache or pull from an internal registry.
[02:24] Connor Liu: that suggests we need two images: one for public registry and one minimal image customers can build in their environment. also need a KV cache persistence note — sometimes transcription here it says 'K V cache' or 'K-V cache' in docs, but it's important we persist local kv state for long conversations to avoid performance drop.
[02:45] Liam O'Neill: and the memory footprint on bare metal is important. what are realistic numbers for a baseline? we don't want to force customers to have 4x32GB GPUs for a connector.
[02:56] Rae Emerson: yes baseline we support small GPU or CPU quantized models. we'll provide recommendations: quantization profile Q4_0 or int8 where applicable. note: this is tradeoff conversation — more quantization reduces memory but impacts quality.
[03:14] Samira Khan: can you run a quick example of how the SAML flow looks with a private deploy? we need to know which entity gets the assertion and where it sits.
[03:24] Connor Liu: sure — whiteboard style: in a private deployment the connector runs in customer network; it should accept SAML assertions via an ingress or sidecar that terminates SAML and exchanges for a short-lived service token. Redwood's control plane (private CP) can broker initial registration but we don't send model requests back through the public control plane if customer chooses full air-gap.
[03:46] Evelyn Park: does Redwood support deploying with our KMS (we use Vault HSM-backed key wraps)? how does key wrapping work with local inference?
[03:56] Rae Emerson: we support a KMS plugin model — in hosted mode we can integrate your KMS via a connector. for on-prem we provide an operator that can call Vault HSM APIs over mTLS. we'll include sample role bindings and KMS policies.
[04:15] Diego Ruiz: can you share the role names / IAM bits? we need to pre-provision roles so our security team can sign off.
[04:22] Maya Patel: action: we'll share a sample IAM manifest and an example Vault policy. i can put that in the workspace.
[04:30] Samira Khan: great. i also want to call out compliance: SOC2 is table stakes. do you have an SOC2 report and pen-test summary to share?
[04:39] Rae Emerson: yes we do. we'll share the SOC 2 Type II letter and our typical audit logs flow. note some customers want extended retention so we'll need to discuss telemetry retention add-on.
[04:54] Liam O'Neill: on the packaging checklist — what does the helm chart look like? will you include an operator?
[05:00] Connor Liu: for marketplace we usually provide: a Helm chart with templated serviceAccount, a CRD if there's lifecycle management, and a CI workflow that builds and signs images. we can include an optional operator for lifecycle/rollouts but keep the base chart lightweight for air-gap installs.
[05:22] Maya Patel: quick clarifying question — do you need automatic model updates from our hosted model catalog, or do you prefer pinned model manifests deployed with the connector?
[05:32] Diego Ruiz: pinned manifests for now. our customers prefer control over model versions. maybe later we can offer a managed update path.
[05:40] Rae Emerson: noted. so we'll provide manifest pinning and a documented rollback procedure.
[05:47] Samira Khan: on performance — we want P95 < 250ms for small text completion workloads. is that realistic with a quantized local model?
[05:56] Connor Liu: depends on sequence length and batching. for small payloads and batching disabled, quantized int8 on a small GPU can reach that. we'll need to run a lab benchmark with your workload to confirm. that's part of our next steps.
[06:12] Diego Ruiz: we have a test harness — i can share a dockerized harness and a sample trace.
[06:18] Maya Patel: perfect. send that to connor and we'll schedule the lab run.
[06:24] Samira Khan: any concerns about multitenancy? we might host multiple customers in a single managed connector instance.
[06:31] Rae Emerson: we recommend tenant isolation via namespace + serviceAccount per tenant, and a per-tenant KV cache namespace. in Dedicated mode customers can have capacity isolation; in Private you control tenancy fully.
[06:48] Evelyn Park: about audit logs — we need structured logs with request id, model version, prompt hash, and masked PII. can you support that?
[06:58] Connor Liu: yes, we can emit structured JSON logs; we also support syslog forwarding or pushing to a sidecar that ships to your SIEM. we'll document the field schema.
[07:12] Diego Ruiz: what about encryption at rest for KV cache? we want the cache encrypted with customer keys.
[07:20] Rae Emerson: we will add a note: KV cache can be encrypted via the local filesystem encryption or via our KMS plugin with envelope encryption. we'll provide config examples.
[07:32] Maya Patel: there's also the marketplace listing flow: we require a partner manifest, screenshots, brief reference arch, and a small integration test. i'll put a sample package link in chat.
[07:44] Samira Khan: do you have a checklist for what the listing needs for Azure/GCP/AWS?
[07:50] Maya Patel: yes — we have a universal packaging guide but we will highlight cloud-specific items (e.g., Azure Managed Identities, GCP service accounts). i'll share the checklist doc after the call.
[07:59] Liam O'Neill: question on signing — you mentioned signed provenance. does Redwood have a distro signing key or should partner sign images?
[08:06] Rae Emerson: partners sign their images and we validate signatures on ingestion. for marketplace we also create an attestation that links the image digest to the listing.
[08:18] Samira Khan: good. can you walk us through a quick end-to-end flow for an enterprise onboarding? maybe a short canary then full rollout.
[08:26] Connor Liu: e2e: 1) partner publishes listing with pinned manifest and Helm chart; 2) we run a verification test in our sandbox; 3) customer deploys to staging using Helm with pinned manifest; 4) run benchmark and smoke tests; 5) canary with 5-10% traffic and metrics validated; 6) full rollout with autoscale triggers. we'll provide a template runbook for this.
[08:51] Diego Ruiz: for canary traffic shaping, do you have router primitives? or should we integrate with service mesh?
[08:58] Rae Emerson: both — we can supply routing hints for our gateway or you can use Istio/Linkerd rules. we'll include examples in the runbook.
[09:08] Samira Khan: about SSO: our customers use SAML IdP and OIDC for machine-to-machine. how would you recommend mapping both?
[09:18] Connor Liu: pattern: use SAML/OIDC at the org boundary for humans and exchange those assertions for short-lived service tokens for the connector and for m2m use OIDC client credentials. put a token broker sidecar or use Plymouth (internal name) — apologies, sometimes the transcription flips internal names — but we'll document both flows.
[09:40] Maya Patel: small note: we'll put links to docs: packaging checklist, helm example repo, SOC2 letter, and KMS integration doc in follow-up email.
[09:49] Samira Khan: thanks. any blockers from your side?
[09:52] Diego Ruiz: none immediate; need to review the sample helm and the role manifests.
[09:57] Evelyn Park: would like to see the audit log schema and confirm PII masking options before security sign-off.
[10:04] Rae Emerson: ok we'll include a sample JSON schema for logs and a masking config example.
[10:10] Maya Patel: let me recap action items... (recap) maya to share packaging checklist and docs, connor helm chart, rae kms + soc2 notes, diego to share traffic traces, evelyn provide security must-haves. schedule lab for week of 6/1.
[10:28] Samira Khan: perfect. thanks y'all.
[10:31] Maya Patel: thanks everyone. we'll follow up with the links and a meeting invite for the benchmark run. bye.
